passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: (Dollars and gallons in thousands, except per share amounts) Please read the following discussion of the Company’s financial condition and results of operations in conjunction with the selected historical consolidated financial data and consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes presented elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Overview As of April 30, 2026, Casey’s General Stores, Inc. and its direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries operate convenience stores primarily under the names "Casey's" and "Casey’s General Store" throughout 19 states, approximately half of which are located in Iowa, Missouri and Illinois. During the third quarter of the prior fiscal year, the Company closed on the acquisition of Fikes Wholesale and Group Petroleum Services (collectively "Fikes"), owner of CEFCO Convenience Stores, which added 198 total stores (the "Fikes acquisition") and a wholesale fuel network. As of April 30, 2026, there were 2,944 stores in operation. Approximately 71% of all stores were opened in areas with populations of fewer than 20,000 persons. The Company competes on the basis of traditional features of convenience store operations such as location, extended hours, product offerings, price and quality of service. All stores carry a broad selection of food items (which at most stores includes, but is not limited to, prepared foods such as regular and breakfast pizza, donuts, hot breakfast items, and hot and cold sandwiches), beverages, tobacco and nicotine products, groceries, health and beauty aids, automotive products, and other non-food items. As of April 30, 2026, 241 store locations offered car washes. In addition, all but six store locations offer fuel. The Company operates a wholesale network where Casey’s manages wholesale fuel supply agreements to certain dealer sites and other wholesale locations. The dealer and wholesale locations are not operated by Casey's and are not included in our overall store count. Approximately 3% of total revenue for the year-ended April 30, 2026 relates to the wholesale fuel network. The Company’s business is seasonal, and generally experiences higher sales and profitability during the first and second fiscal quarters (May-October), when the weather is warmer across our footprint and guests tend to purchase greater quantities of fuel and certain convenience items such as beer, sports drinks, water, soft drinks and ice. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider the risks described in this report before making a decision to invest in our securities. If any of such risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, and/or results of operations could be materially adversely affected. In that case, the trading price of our securities could decline and you might lose all or part of your investment. Risks Related to Our Business Operations Our business and our reputation could be adversely affected by a cyber or data security incident or the failure to protect sensitive guest, Team Member or supplier data, or the failure to comply with applicable regulations relating to data security and privacy. In the normal course of our business, we obtain, are provided and have access to large amounts of personal data, including but not limited to credit and debit card information, personally identifiable information and other data from and about our guests, Team Members, and suppliers. A compromise or a breach in our systems, or another data security or privacy incident that results in the loss, unauthorized release, disclosure or acquisition of such data or information, or other sensitive data or information, or other internal or external cyber or data security threats, including but not limited to viruses, denial-of-service attacks, phishing attacks, social engineering attacks, ransomware attacks and other intentional or unintentional disruptions, could occur and have a material adverse effect on our operations and ability to operate, reputation, operating results and financial condition. The rapid evolution and increased adoption of artificial intelligence technologies may also heighten our cybersecurity risks by making cyber-attacks more difficult to detect, contain, and mitigate. In addition, similar events at vendors, third-party service providers or other market participants, whether or not we are directly impacted, could negatively affect our business and supply chain or lead to a general loss of guest confidence, which could result in reduced guest traffic and sales. A data security or privacy incident of any kind could expose us to risk in terms of the loss, unauthorized release, disclosure or acquisition of sensitive guest, Team Member or supplier data, and could result in litigation or other regulatory action being brought against us and damages, monetary and other claims made by or on behalf of the payment card brands, guests, Team Members, shareholders, financial institutions and governmental agencies, or monetary demands or other extortion attempts from cybercriminals. Such events could give rise to substantial monetary damages and/or losses which are not covered, or in some instances fully covered, by our insurance policies and which could adversely affect our reputation, results of operations, financial condition and liquidity. credit_strengths.text: Casey's operates a large, geographically dense convenience-store and fuel network with a growing wholesale fuel supply business, and revenue has expanded steadily across the three fiscal years shown. This scale and store-level density support stable in-store margins and fuel volumes, giving the issuer a defensible cash-generative retail platform despite competition from larger national chains.

Operating cash flow has risen each year and comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving meaningful free cash flow after maintenance and growth spending. Cash generation is the primary support for the capital structure, and the cash-flow-to-debt ratio sits above the sector median, indicating better internal funding capacity than typical consumer discretionary peers.

key_risks.text: The disclosed risk factors highlight cyber and data-security exposure from large volumes of guest payment and personal data, with potential litigation, card-brand claims and uninsured losses. Artificial intelligence is noted as heightening detection and containment difficulty. Such an incident could disrupt operations, damage reputation and require significant remediation spending, pressuring liquidity and cash flow.

Debt maturities are weighted toward later years, but the issuer still faces meaningful near-term repayments alongside scheduled shareholder distributions and acquisition spending. Dividends and buybacks together absorb a substantial share of free cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity if operating cash flow softens or capital expenditure remains elevated.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest expense is modest relative to operating cash flow, and cash on hand plus internally generated funds cover the next twelve months of maturities. However, operating income is not available in the bundle, so interest coverage and EBITDA-based leverage cannot be computed. This data gap is material because it prevents a full assessment of earnings-based debt-service capacity.

The current ratio is close to parity, with current assets only marginally exceeding current liabilities, so working-capital flexibility is limited. Free cash flow to debt is above the sector median, but the ratio relies on continued operating cash flow growth. A decline in cash generation would reduce headroom against the cash-flow threshold used in the indicative risk profile.

overall_credit_view.text: Casey's presents a cash-generative retail credit with revenue growth, rising operating cash flow and free cash flow that covers capital spending. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal on the single available cash-flow ratio, but the absence of operating income and EBITDA prevents a complete leverage and coverage assessment. The credit view is therefore constructive but constrained by disclosure gaps.

Analyst judgement: leverage and coverage metrics cannot be benchmarked against sector medians without operating income, so the comparative position is uncertain. The debt maturity profile is manageable, but shareholder distributions and acquisitions consume most free cash flow, limiting deleveraging. Continued cash-flow growth and disciplined capital allocation are needed to preserve the current risk profile.

credit_strengths.text: Casey's 營運一個規模龐大、地理密度高的便利店及燃料網絡，並擁有持續增長的批發燃料供應業務，而收入在所示的三個財政年度內穩步擴張。此規模及門店密度支持穩定的店內利潤率及燃料銷量，令發行人儘管面對來自大型全國連鎖店的競爭，仍擁有具防禦性的現金生成零售平台。
營運現金流逐年上升，並足以從容覆蓋資本開支，在維持性及增長性支出後留下有意義的自由現金流。現金生成是資本結構的主要支撐，而現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，顯示其內部融資能力優於典型的非必需消費品同業。

key_risks.text: 所披露的風險因素凸顯來自大量客戶支付及個人數據的網絡及數據安全風險，並可能引發訴訟、信用卡品牌索賠及未投保損失。人工智能被指出會加大偵測及遏制的難度。此類事件可能中斷營運、損害聲譽，並需要大量補救支出，對流動性及現金流構成壓力。
債務到期日偏重於較後年份，但發行人仍面臨有意義的近期還款，同時須應付既定股東分派及收購支出。股息與回購合共佔用相當大比例的自由現金流，若營運現金流轉弱或資本開支維持高企，將限制去槓桿能力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息支出相對於營運現金流而言不大，而手頭現金加上內部產生資金足以覆蓋未來十二個月的到期債務。然而，資料組合中並無營運收入，因此無法計算利息覆蓋率及以 EBITDA 為基礎的槓桿。此數據缺口屬重大，因其妨礙對以盈利為基礎的債務償付能力作出全面評估。
流動比率接近持平，流動資產僅略高於流動負債，因此營運資金靈活性有限。自由現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，但該比率依賴營運現金流持續增長。現金生成一旦下降，將減少相對於指示性風險狀況所用現金流門檻的緩衝空間。

overall_credit_view.text: Casey's 呈現一個具現金生成能力的零售信用，收入增長、營運現金流上升，且自由現金流足以覆蓋資本開支。根據唯一可得的現金流比率，指示性財務風險狀況為極低，但缺乏營運收入及 EBITDA 令槓桿及覆蓋率評估無法完整進行。因此，信用觀點屬建設性，但受披露缺口所限制。
分析師判斷：在沒有營運收入的情況下，槓桿及覆蓋率指標無法與行業中位數作基準比較，因此相對位置並不明確。債務到期結構屬可控，但股東分派及收購消耗大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿。需要持續的現金流增長及嚴守紀律的資本配置，方能維持目前的風險狀況。
